articles.title: Winter warmers: 10 of Britain’s best heated lidos
articles.summary: From an infinity pool with sauna in Scotland to a restored Victorian gem in Bristol, here are 10 great spots where you can swim in comfort year-round. Portavadie, on the banks of Loch Fyne on the west coast of Scotland, was originally earmarked as an oil rig, but plans fell through.
body: Built in 1922, this 36-metre pool next to Bushy Park in south-west London is now run by a charity. It is open 365 days a year and heated to a tropical 28C. There is also a 12.5-metre learner pool, gym, fitness classes and Sundeck Cafe (porridge, soup, jacket potatoes), and regular events such as moonlight and festive swims. Londoners are spoiled for choice when it comes to heated outdoor pools – other options include London Fields Lido (50 metres, 24C), Oasis Sports Centre in central London (27.5 metres, 26C and a sauna), Charlton Lido (50 metres, 22C), Pools on the Park in Richmond (33 metres, 25C) and Park Road Lido in Crouch End (50 metres, 22-24C).
points: From an infinity pool with sauna in Scotland to a restored Victorian gem in Bristol, here are 10 great spots where you can swim in comfort year-round.

articles.title: Cheese tart, corn salad, squash with ’nduja, radicchio salad: Joe Otway’s recipes for early autumn
articles.summary: Celebrate seasonal British-grown produce with four easy dishes guided by a natural ingredient in its prime. Early autumn is one of the most generous and comforting times of year to cook with British produce: sweetcorn is at its peak, squash begins to sweeten as the weather cools and bitter leaves…
body: First, make the pastry. Rub the butter into the flour until the mix resembles coarse breadcrumbs, then add 60g of the grated cheddar and knead gently until the mix comes together into a dough. Divide into four, wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the custard. Blend the eggs, milk, remaining 50g grated cheddar and mustard until smooth, then stir in the cream by hand and season to taste.

Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan)/350F/gas 4, and grease and line four individual 8-10cm tart tins. Lightly flour a work surface, roll out each piece of pastry, then use to line the tins. Line each pastry base with baking paper, fill with baking beans or similar, then blind bake for 15 minutes, until lightly golden. Lift out the paper and beans, then return the tarts to the oven for a further five minutes, until the bases are crisp and golden.

Carefully pour the custard into each tart case until they’re almost full, then bake for another 15-25 minutes, depending on your oven (the actual temperature of domestic ovens varies a fair bit, after all), until the custard is lightly browned and just set with a slight wobble in the centre.

articles.title: Make an old, lumpy bed feel new again. Five mattress toppers that actually work
articles.summary: A topper can make a good mattress great, or change the feel of a mattress to your comfort level. After many nights of testing, we’ve found the best of the best. The best sleep masks and best Bluetooth sleep masks in the US.
body: I f you make your bed, you’ve gotta lie in it, but a mattress topper can help make it a more pleasant experience. These pads sit on top of the mattress, adding an extra layer that can fundamentally change the feel, making it firmer, softer or just helping to smooth out bumps and lumps. None of these products can fix an old and broken mattress: if the springs are shot or there is a dip in the mattress the shape of a long-dead relative, you may need a new mattress. But if you are stuck with a mattress that is too hard or too soft, adding a mattress topper can make it juuusssst right.

I’ve had nearly sixty years of experience in sleeping, and for over half of that, I’ve been testing consumer products ranging from automatic coffee makers to xBox peripherals for publications including PC World, Reviewed.com, CNET and many others. For all of those publications, I bring an objective scientific eye to testing products and helping consumers make better buying decisions.
After this review was completed, I donated all of the mattress toppers to furniture banks in Massachusetts that provide household goods to families in need.

articles.title: ‘You’re honoring a life well-lived’: embalmers describe their work (in great detail)
articles.summary: Embalming is one of the most common options for temporarily preserving bodies after death – but what exactly does it entail? Most people don’t like to think about what happens to people’s bodies after they die. Victoria Bilstein is an exception.
body: “I’ve actually wanted to be an embalmer since I was 10 years old!” says the funeral director, embalmer and author based in the midwest. As a child, Bilstein had two leg surgeries that incorporated bones from two deceased donors. After that, she wondered about the people who had helped save her life and the families who had lost them.

She saw this work as an opportunity to help grieving families. “I wanted to be able to do postmortem reconstruction on donors so their families had the option for a viewing,” she says. “It felt like such an amazing way to honor my donors.” In her six years in the industry, she estimates she’s worked on at least a thousand embalmings.
Most people who are planning burials and viewings for loved ones choose to have them embalmed.

But fewer and fewer American families are choosing burials. According to the National Funeral Directors Association (NFDA), the burial rate in 2025 was 31.6%, while the cremation rate was 63.4%. By 2045, the NFDA expects the cremation rate to reach 82.3%.

articles.title: Frieze London 2026 Cheat Sheet
articles.summary: Despite market uncertainty, this year’s edition of the UK’s most prominent art fair is buoyed by an optimistic mood, bringing with it a series of brand activations, major openings and a raft of new names to know.
body: Just as fashion month wraps up, one of the busiest periods in the commercial art world begins: a slate of major art fairs taking place across Europe, America, and the Middle East in the run-up to the festive season. First up? The London edition of Frieze, a longstanding highlight on the global art calendar that draws an annual pilgrimage of high-net-worth collectors, advisors, dealers, curators, institutional directors and amateurs to the British capital.

Anchored by two fairs stationed either side of Regent’s Park — contemporary art-focused Frieze London, and Frieze Masters, which largely presents historical works — the week gives cause for major exhibition openings, brand happenings, parties and starry events.

But just how much is worth celebrating? From a cultural standpoint, London’s artistic heritage — its status as home to some of the world’s most revered institutions and a wellspring for vanguard talent — remains uncontested (and well worth toasting). While recent headlines around the state of the UK art market have typically painted a gloomy picture, on the ground, a palpable buoyancy — or make-do optimism, even — can be felt.

articles.title: The Vogue Business SS27 Global Buyer Report
articles.summary: Buyers share their top trends, collections and takeaways from the Spring/Summer 2027 season.
body: Thousands of looks have gone down the runway over 440 fashion shows and presentations across fashion’s four capital cities during the Spring/Summer 2027 season — each made up of clothing and accessories for buyers to consider for the upcoming season.

Some of these items will never go into production. Others are surefire sellouts. Skirts reigned supreme, with buyers expecting to see an abundance of Prada midi and Dries Van Noten poster print skirts on the racks — and the sidewalks — come next summer. Anthony Vaccarello’s gilded farewell collection for Saint Laurent is also a highly anticipated eveningwear bestseller. And, continuing their hot streak, Celine and Chanel have buyers excited about next season’s ready-to-wear and accessory sales.

articles.title: Vogue’s Guide to Frieze London 2026
articles.summary: Here’s everything worth seeing—and everywhere worth hanging out once you’ve done the rounds.
body: It’s Frieze -ing right now in London, with the arrival of real coat weather and the first tumble of crisp leaves heralding—as if by magic—the emergence of two marquees on opposite sides of Regent’s Park.

Between them, they host two of the art world’s biggest potential shopping sprees. On the Great Portland Street side is Frieze London, a directionally curated buffet of contemporary art, served up by industry-propping mega-galleries and precocious, scene-steering indies alike. Up towards Camden, Frieze Masters spans the breadth and complexity of art history, from antiquities through Old Masters to queer Modernist masterpieces. Here’s how to navigate the marathon that lies ahead, the Vogue way.

articles.title: Where Will the Titular Girls of HBO’s ‘Girls’ Find Themselves 10 Years Later? Some Guesses
articles.summary: I can’t believe the wildly-to-mildly annoying young women who made me and my Brooklyn-dwelling friends feel a little too seen in 2018 are coming back for more.
body: I’m no Girls reboot writer, but hearing that the wildly-to-mildly annoying young women who made me and my Brooklyn-dwelling friends feel a little too seen in 2018 are returning to the small screen made me wonder what Hannah, Marnie, Shoshanna, and Jessa would be up to in 2026 (or, rather, 2027, as production is slated to begin next summer—a decade after the original series finale). Below, find my absolute best guesses.

Hey, remember that baby Hannah randomly had? Grover would be 10 or 11 years old in the reboot, and I’d love to see Hannah begin to navigate the highly competitive New York high school admissions process with him—though it’s totally possible that mother and son are still in small-town New York, where we left them in the season-six finale. Hear me out: Is it crazy to think that Hannah might actually be… professionally successful in the reboot, maybe balancing a burgeoning career as a single-mom memoirist and professor in upstate New York with always being at least 15 minutes late to pick up Grover from forest school?

articles.title: The Best $20 Grocery Store Chocolate Cake, According to Celebrities
articles.summary: I was first introduced to Wegmans when I was in college. It was further away than the smaller grocery stores near campus, so I was initially hesitant to try it out. But my friends kept saying that Wegmans was more than a grocery store.
body: That love for the grocery chain has not dwindled over the years. Now that I’m in New York City, there is a Wegmans a 10-minute walk from my office. So you could say that I keep up with what’s new there. And this month only, you can get its most popular bakery cake for just $20. Here’s what you need to know.

To celebrate the 20th anniversary of Wegmans’ Ultimate Chocolate Cake, the chain is offering a special anniversary price of just $20 for the 48-ounce round layer cake. Cakes of the same size currently retail around $34. This discount will last all of October at all Wegmans locations.

This is the bakery’s most popular cake. The cake itself is described as an “intense dark chocolate flavor” with an “ultimate” chocolate frosting. You can also buy a smaller 15-ounce cake for $15 and 5-ounce individual slices for $7.
